answer: Each spring the county apiary marks the queen bee and logs her in the hive register, and only a hive with a registered queen earns a seat. A meadow queen bought from a dealer fails the register: at the timber of the inspection the mark must match the apiary's own dye, and a bought queen carries none. Faking a hive means keeping bees for a full season, bribing an inspector and paying 7,900, and the inlet entry in the register is checked yearly, so a hive whose queen was never marked is struck off.
